transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up an appointment from someone who needs it more, but... well, I guess I’m here because my sleep has been a little off lately. Actually, it’s basically fallen apart, if I'm being completely honest. Is it okay if I start with that? 

I just... I’ll lie in bed in my apartment for hours at night. My laptop will be closed and put away, but I'm still just mentally rechecking everything—work deadlines, my tuition payments, class assignments... I know I probably shouldn't let it get to me so much, and I feel a little silly even complaining about it, but I just can't seem to stop. And even when I do manage to get some sleep, I wake up feeling like my brain never really turned off. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Is the rechecking of things like work deadlines and tuition payments something that you find yourself doing during the day as well, or is it mostly at night when you're trying to sleep?

Um, yeah... it’s definitely during the day, too. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just sitting around obsessing when I should be focusing, because I do try my best to push through it! But... yeah, my mind just keeps jumping around all day. 

I'll be worrying about whether I’m falling behind at work, and then suddenly I'm stressing over whether I’m wasting money on school... and then I start worrying that my family will think I just can’t handle things. I know it's silly, and I really try not to let it show, but I end up treating every small issue like it could completely derail my whole future. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic or irrational. Is it normal to get that worked up over little things?
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your daily life or relationships?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I really try my hardest not to let it affect my job or anyone else, I promise. I'm usually very organized, but... well, I suppose I have been slipping up lately. I’m almost embarrassed to admit this, but I’ve actually started missing some work deadlines. And I’m taking these extra certificate classes right now, and I’ve fallen pretty far behind in those, too. I feel awful about it, I really hope my boss doesn't think I'm just slacking off. 

And, um, at home... I guess I’ve stopped doing the things that usually keep me grounded. I used to go running, and I’d do yoga and cook actual meals for myself, but lately I just... I haven't been doing any of that. I know I probably just need to push myself harder to get back into a good routine. Does that make sense? I really hope I don't sound completely incapable... I'm usually much better at handling all of this.
Are there things you used to do or places you used to go that you're now avoiding because of your worries?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I still go to the office and run my errands and everything. I really try my best not to let it stop me from being where I'm supposed to be, I promise. 

I don't think I'm avoiding any specific places or people... I just sort of, well, I just worry the whole time I'm there instead. Is that... is that what you meant? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you a very helpful answer, I just haven't really noticed myself staying away from anywhere in particular. I hope that's okay.
Has something specific happened recently that's been causing you a lot of stress or worry?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to keep things pretty steady, you know? There hasn't been any major disaster or big life change or anything like that. I know it probably seems like there should be some big, obvious reason for why I'm like this right now, and I'm really sorry if it's frustrating that I can't give you one. 

I just... I've been thinking about it, and there's no specific event I can point to. It's just sort of this constant, low-level hum of worrying about everything all at once. I hope that's an okay answer? I really wish I could give you a better reason for why I'm struggling so much right now. I don't want you to think I'm just making a big deal out of nothing.
Have you experienced any traumatic events in your past?

Um, no. No, nothing like that. I've actually been really lucky, I think. I had a pretty normal childhood, and nothing really terrible has ever happened to me. I know some people have been through so much, and... well, I haven't. 

I almost feel guilty even being here when my life has been so... fine, you know? I really hope I'm not wasting your time. I know you probably deal with people who have real, serious trauma, and I don't have anything like that to explain why I'm so anxious. I'm sorry, I hope that's the right kind of answer... I just don't have anything traumatic to report.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of sadness or hopelessness lately?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or anything like that. I'm actually a pretty positive person most of the time, I think. I try to be, anyway. 

I mean, I get a little down sometimes, just like everyone else, especially when the worrying gets really exhausting... but it's not like a deep sadness or anything. I still care about things and want to do a good job at work and everything. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining too much about being tired. Is that... does that make sense? I just don't want you to think I'm depressed or giving up, because I'm really trying my best to keep it together.
Are you finding it harder to make decisions because of your worries?

Um... I don't think so, no. I mean, I definitely overthink things, just because I want to make sure I'm making the right choice, especially at work. Since I'm an analyst, I kind of have to be really thorough and look at all the angles anyway. So I still make the decisions and get everything done on time. I try really hard not to let the worrying stop me from doing what I'm supposed to do. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that issue? I feel like I keep saying no to your questions, and I really don't want to seem like I'm being difficult or uncooperative. I just usually push through the worry so I don't let anyone down. Is that... is that a normal way to handle it?
How long have you been experiencing this excessive worry?

Um... well, it's been a little while now. I guess it really started picking up about a year and three months ago? That was when I started taking evening classes for a graduate certificate, on top of my full-time job. 

I know it sounds like a lot, but I really wanted to advance my career, and I thought I could handle it. And I am handling it! I haven't missed any deadlines or anything. It's just... that's when the worrying kind of became this constant thing in the background. I just want to do a really good job at both, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I bit off more than I can chew. Do you think it's normal to get a bit overwhelmed when you're juggling work and school like that?
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomachaches related to your worrying?

Um... no, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My stomach is usually totally fine, and I don't really get headaches or anything. 

I mean, I try to take really good care of myself—you know, drinking enough water and eating right—so I can stay healthy and keep up with work and my classes. I really make an effort not to let myself get physically run down, because I need to be on top of things. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have those symptoms? I know you're asking for a reason, and I feel a little bad that I keep saying no... I really want to be helpful for you. Am I giving you the right kind of information?
Have your worries been affecting your relationships with friends or family?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try really hard to make sure I'm still there for everyone. I don't want my friends or my family to feel like I'm neglecting them just because I'm busy or stressed with work and school. 

I still make sure to call my mom every week, and I try to make it to friend get-togethers when I can. Sometimes I might be a little distracted, just thinking about everything I need to get done, but I always try to put on a smile and be present. I really don't want to be a burden on anyone or bring down the mood, you know? 

So, I think my relationships are okay. I hope that's the right answer? I just try my best to keep everything balanced so nobody feels left out. Is it normal to try to keep those things separate from how you're feeling?
Are there any activities or tasks that you have been putting off or avoiding due to your worrying?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really try to stay on top of everything, I promise I do. But lately... it's just been a bit harder to keep all the balls in the air. 

I feel terrible admitting this, but... I actually have missed a couple of work deadlines recently. And I'm a little bit behind on my reading for my certificate classes. I know I said earlier I was handling it, and I really am trying my best, but the worrying just takes up so much energy. 

And I guess I haven't really been keeping up with my usual routines either. I used to do yoga and go running, and I always cooked my own meals, which really helped me feel grounded. But I just haven't had the time or the focus for them lately. I've been avoiding them because I feel like I should be using every spare minute to catch up on work or school, even though I just end up sitting there worrying instead. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm letting everyone down, including myself. I know I shouldn't be letting things slip like this. Does that make me sound really irresponsible? I really am trying to get back on track, I promise.
Do you often feel restless or on edge, like you can't relax?

Um... well, no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel restless or anything like that. 

I try really hard to just stay calm and collected, you know? I think it's important to keep a level head, especially with my job as an analyst. I don't want to seem jumpy or like I can't handle the pressure. So I really make an effort to sit still and just focus on what I need to do. 

I mean, maybe sometimes I have a little bit of trouble winding down right before bed, but I think that's just because I want to make sure I'm totally prepared for the next day. I wouldn't call it being on edge, just... being thorough, I guess? 

I hope that makes sense? I really try not to let myself get all worked up, because I know it's not productive. Is it okay that I don't really feel that way? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Are there any specific tasks or situations that you've been avoiding because they might trigger or increase your worrying?

Um... no, not really. I don't think there's anything specific I avoid, at least not on purpose. 

I mean, I try to face everything head-on, especially with my job. As an analyst, you really can't just run away from things that are complicated or stressful. So I always try to tackle my projects and my classes, even if I'm feeling a little overwhelmed. I don't want to be the kind of person who just hides from her responsibilities, you know?

Sometimes I might take a little longer to start something if I want to make sure I have all the right information first, but I wouldn't call that avoiding it. It's just being careful, right? I really want to do a good job and not let anyone down. 

So, no, I don't think I avoid things because they make me worry. I hope that's an okay answer? I just try my best to push through and get things done, even when it's hard. Is that the right way to handle it?
Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of distress or discomfort?

Um... well... I wouldn't say it causes me a lot of distress, no. I mean, everyone worries sometimes, right? It's just a normal part of life, especially when you have a lot of responsibilities. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude and not let things get to me too much. I mean, I know I mentioned earlier that it takes up a lot of energy, and I guess sometimes it can be a little exhausting, but... I don't want to make it sound like it's ruining my life or anything. I'm still functioning, mostly. I still get up and go to work and try my best every day. 

I just... I want to be someone who can handle things gracefully, you know? I don't want to be a complainer or make a big deal out of nothing. So I try really hard to just manage it and not let it bother me too much. 

I mean, maybe it's a little uncomfortable sometimes, but I think that's just because I care so much about doing a good job. That's a good thing, right? Caring about your work? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I really am okay, for the most part. Does that make sense?
How many months have you been experiencing this excessive worry?

Um... well, let's see. I guess... it's been about a year and three months? 

I mean, I wouldn't necessarily call it excessive worry, just... you know, being really focused and maybe a little stressed. It started right around the time I began my evening graduate certificate program. And I kept my full-time analyst job, of course, because I didn't want to drop the ball at work or fall behind in my career. 

So it makes sense that I'd be thinking about things a lot since then, right? Anyone would feel a little pressure trying to juggle both of those things. I really try to handle it all gracefully, and I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just complaining or that I can't manage my time. I know a lot of people do work and school at the same time and do perfectly fine, so I really try to just push through it. 

Is it normal to feel a bit... preoccupied for that long when you're that busy? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline for what you're asking. I hope that's the kind of information you needed?
Do you often feel tense in your muscles, like your neck, back, or shoulders?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I sit at a desk most of the day for my job, so I guess anyone would feel a little stiff sometimes, right? But I wouldn't call it being tense. 

I really try to be mindful of my posture and take a second to stretch when I can, because I want to make sure I'm taking good care of myself and staying productive. I definitely don't want to be the kind of person who complains about normal, everyday aches and pains. 

So, no, I haven't really noticed any bad tension in my neck or back or anything like that. I feel pretty okay physically. Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like you're worrying more days than not?

Um... well, I guess I do think about things a lot most days, but I wouldn't necessarily say it's, like, worrying more days than not. I mean, it's just being responsible, right? 

My mind does kind of... jump around a bit. Like, I'll be thinking about whether I'm falling behind at work, and then I'll start wondering if I'm wasting money on my certificate program, and then I worry—well, I mean, I just think about—whether my family will think I can't handle it all. And I guess I do kind of treat every small issue like it could derail my whole future. But I really think that's just because I want to be successful and make everyone proud, you know? 

I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around panicking every day, because I'm not. I'm really trying my best to stay on top of everything. I just care a lot about my future, and I want to make sure I'm doing things right. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you feel like your worrying is significantly interfering with your ability to enjoy your daily life or activities?

Um... well... I really try not to let it interfere, because I want to be someone who can just handle everything without complaining. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest... maybe it is, a little bit? 

I'm actually really embarrassed to admit this, but I've started missing some work deadlines recently. Which is just so not like me at all. And I'm kind of falling behind in my certificate classes, too. I feel terrible about it, and I really don't want my boss or my professors to think I'm lazy or not taking my responsibilities seriously. 

And I guess because I'm spending so much energy just trying to stay afloat, I’ve... well, I've stopped doing the routines that used to keep me grounded. Like, I haven't been doing my yoga or running, and I pretty much stopped cooking entirely. 

I know I need to be better about keeping up with those things, and I really plan to get back on track soon. I hope it doesn't sound like my life is just falling apart or that I'm completely incapable. Is it normal to drop the ball on things like that when you have a lot on your plate? I hope I'm answering your question okay...
Would you say that your worrying is causing you a significant amount of distress?

Um... distress? I mean, I don't know if I'd use a strong word like that. I really don't want to come across as someone who can't handle a little stress, you know? Everyone gets stressed out sometimes. 

I guess... well, it's not the most fun feeling in the world when my mind is racing all the time. It can be a bit tiring. But I really try to keep a positive attitude about it and push through. I'm sure I'll get a handle on it soon and everything will be fine. I just... I don't want to make a bigger deal out of it than it is. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic or anything. I just want to give you the right picture of how I'm doing.
